newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba launches slim CD-ROM drive for notebooks.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba launches slim CD-ROM drive for notebooks.

text.p: Japan's Toshiba Corp launched a new, super-slim CD-ROM drive for notebook computers on Monday which it said brings their performance into line with desktops.
The company also said it had launched two other CD-ROM drives for desktop computers. All three models went on sale in Japan and the United States on Monday.

The drive for notebook computers, with an average 10-times rotational speed, is 12.7 mm (0.5 inch) thick and can read an average of 1,500 kilobytes of data a second while using little electric power, Toshiba said in a statement.
The compact, high-speed drive brings to portable computers a level of CD-ROM (compact disc read-only memory) performance previously limited to desktop personal computers, it said.

The two other new drives are 41.5 mm (1.6 inches) thick, offering a maximum 12-times rotational speed and a data transfer rate of 1,800 kilobytes per second, providing desktop computers with enhanced levels of performance, Toshiba said.
The CD-ROM drive market is enjoying considerable growth, with demand expected to rise 25 percent to more than 40 million units worldwide in the fiscal year to March 1997, it said.
The trend is towards high-performance CD-ROMs slim enough to be used in ever-smaller portable personal computers, it added.
Toshiba said samples of the CD-ROM drive for notebook computers were priced at 60,000 yen ($535) in Japan.
The two drives for desktop computers were priced at 50,000 yen ($446) and 60,000 yen ($535).
CD-ROMs can carry large amounts of multimedia data.
